extracted.intended_audience: Users of PARI/GP (mathematicians, computational number theorists, and developers using the PARI library)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for PARI/GP arithmetic and finite-field library functions: usage, parameters, return formats, algorithmic choices and caveats for number-theory computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: factorint: integer factoring engine access & flags
rubrics_metrics.description: Gives direct access to the integer factoring engine called by most arithmetical functions. flag is optional; its binary digits mean 1: avoid MPQS, 2: skip first stage ECM (we may still fall back to it later), 4: avoid Rho and SQUFOF, 8: don’t run final ECM (as a result, a huge composite may be declared to be prime). Note that a (strong) probabilistic primality test is used; thus composites might not be detected, although no example is known.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may set factor_proven default to 1 to force proven primes. Use isprime on factors if you want to guarantee primality. Use gp's debug parameter to inspect internals (level 3 outline, 4 time keeping, 5+ increasing internal details). Library syntax: GEN factorint(GEN x, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: factormod: factor polynomial over finite field (D options)
rubrics_metrics.description: Factors the polynomial f over the finite field defined by domain D. D may be: a prime p for Fp; [T,p] for Fp[x]/(T); a t_FFELT (attached field); or omitted to use the field of definition of f (must be a finite field). Result is a two-column matrix: first column irreducible polynomials dividing f, second their exponents. Irreducible factors are ordered by increasing degree and result is canonical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conventions: 0 polynomial factors as 0^1; non-zero constant polynomial has empty factorization (0x2 matrix). If flag non-zero, outputs only degrees (in increasing order) which may differ in ordering from flag=0 when multiplicities present. Library syntax: GEN factormod0(GEN f, GEN D = NULL, long flag). Examples in documentation illustrate use over F3 and extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: factormodDDF: distinct-degree factorization
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinct-degree factorization of a squarefree polynomial f over the finite field defined by D (same D options as factormod). Result is a two-column matrix: first column monic squarefree pairwise coprime polynomials dividing f whose irreducible factors all have degree d; second column contains the degrees of the irreducible factors. Factors ordered by increasing degree and result is canonical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Somewhat faster than full factorization. Examples show timing comparisons; library syntax: GEN factormodDDF(GEN f, GEN D = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: factormodSQF: squarefree factorization
rubrics_metrics.description: Squarefree factorization of polynomial f over finite field defined by D (same D options). Result: two-column matrix, first column monic squarefree pairwise coprime polynomials dividing f; second column contains the power to which the polynomial divides f. Factors ordered by increasing degree and result is canonical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Faster than full factorization for inputs with powers. Examples and timing comparisons provided. Library syntax: GEN factormodSQF(GEN f, GEN D = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: ffcompomap: compose finite-field maps
rubrics_metrics.description: Given f: k→l and g: l→m (partial maps between finite fields), return the partial map f o g from k to m.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples demonstrate composition/inversion identities. Library syntax: GEN ffcompomap(GEN f, GEN g).

rubrics_metrics.name: ffembed: embed definition field of a into definition field of b
rubrics_metrics.description: Given finite-field elements a and b, return a map embedding the definition field of a into the definition field of b, assuming latter contains former.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows the image preserves minimal polynomial. Library syntax: GEN ffembed(GEN a, GEN b).

rubrics_metrics.name: ffextend: extend field by root of irreducible polynomial
rubrics_metrics.description: Extend the field K of definition of a by a root of polynomial P ∈ K[X] assumed irreducible over K. Return [r, m] where r is a root in extension L and m is a map from K to L. Optional v sets variable name for display.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generator of L can be recovered with ffgen(r). Image of P in L[X] via ffmap(m,P). Library syntax: GEN ffextend(GEN a, GEN P, long v = -1).

rubrics_metrics.name: fffrobenius: Frobenius map power
rubrics_metrics.description: Return the n-th power of the Frobenius map over the field of definition of m (default n=1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show ffmap(fffrobenius(a),a) = a^p. Library syntax: GEN fffrobenius(GEN m, long n).

rubrics_metrics.name: ffgen: finite-field generator construction and conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Return a generator for finite field k as a t_FFELT. k can be given by its order q, the pair [p,f], a monic irreducible polynomial modulo a prime, or a t_FFELT. Optional v sets display variable name. When only order specified, generator is deterministic (ffinit polynomial used).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For efficiency characteristic is not checked prime; if polynomial given, irreducibility not checked. To obtain multiplicative generator call ffprimroot on result. Library syntax: GEN ffgen(GEN k, long v = -1).

rubrics_metrics.name: ffinit: compute monic irreducible polynomial over Fp
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes a monic polynomial of degree n irreducible over Fp (p assumed prime). Uses a fast variant of Adleman-Lenstra's algorithm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful with ffgen. Library syntax: GEN ffinit(GEN p, long n, long v = -1).

rubrics_metrics.name: ffinvmap: inverse partial map between finite fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Given m a map from K to L two finite fields, return partial map p from L to K such that for all k in K, p(m(k)) = k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates inversion and round-trip property on polynomials. Library syntax: GEN ffinvmap(GEN m).

rubrics_metrics.name: fflog: discrete logarithm in finite field (algorithms & options)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discrete logarithm of finite-field element x in base g, returning e with g^e = x. Optional o represents multiplicative order of g; preferred format [ord, factor(ord)].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses combination of generic discrete log algorithms (znlog), cubic-sieve index calculus for large fields degree ≥5, Coppersmith's algorithm for characteristic ≤5. If o omitted assume g primitive. Result undefined if e does not exist. Library syntax: GEN fflog(GEN x, GEN g, GEN o = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: ffmap: apply finite-field map to element
rubrics_metrics.description: Given partial map m between two finite fields, return image of x by m. Applied recursively to vectors, matrices, polynomials. If m undefined at x, return [].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserves polynomial discriminant under mapping (example). Library syntax: GEN ffmap(GEN m, GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: ffnbirred / ffsumnbirred: count monic irreducible polynomials
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes the number of monic irreducible polynomials over Fq of degree exactly n (flag=0) or at most n (flag=1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntaxes include ffnbirred0, ffnbirred (flag=0) and ffsumnbirred (flag=1).

rubrics_metrics.name: fforder: multiplicative order in finite field (use of optional o)
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiplicative order of finite-field element x. Optional o is a multiple of the order (preferred format [N, factor(N)] where N is cardinality of multiplicative group).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing o can speed computation significantly. Examples show orders with and without providing o and timing difference. Library syntax: GEN fforder(GEN x, GEN o = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: ffprimroot: find primitive root of finite-field multiplicative group
rubrics_metrics.description: Return a primitive root of multiplicative group of definition field of finite-field element x. Optional &o set to [ord, factor(ord)].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The factorization vector o is useful for fflog/fforder. Library syntax: GEN ffprimroot(GEN x, GEN *o = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: gcd: greatest common divisor across many types & algorithm choices
rubrics_metrics.description: Creates gcd(x,y). Works on many types including rational numbers; if y omitted and x vector returns gcd of components. When vectors/matrices involved gcd is applied recursively with type-preserving rules; gcd not commutative on these types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algorithm choices: naive Euclid except integers use modified right-shift binary; univariate polynomials over same number field use modular gcd; general polynomials use subresultant algorithm when coefficient explosion likely. For inexact-coefficient polynomials gcd is scalar; use polresultant to check near-triviality and gcdext for approximate gcd with u,v. Library syntax: GEN ggcd0(GEN x, GEN y = NULL) and variants.

rubrics_metrics.name: gcdext: extended gcd (u,v,d) with inexact-coefficient behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns [u,v,d] with d = gcd(x,y) and x*u + y*v = d; arguments must be integers or polynomials. For inexact-coefficient polynomials compute u,v,d such that x*u + y*v = d where d approximately divides both inputs (outputs not mathematically well-defined but useful to check approximations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show different outputs for inexact inputs. Use to check approximation closeness. Library syntax: GEN gcdext0(GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: hilbert: Hilbert symbol
rubrics_metrics.description: Hilbert symbol of x and y modulo prime p, with p=0 meaning infinite place. If p omitted, choice depends on types (p=0 for rationals/reals; p=q if one arg is t_INTMOD modulo q or q-adic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incompatible types raise error. Library syntax: long hilbert(GEN x, GEN y, GEN p = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: isfundamental: test for fundamental discriminant
rubrics_metrics.description: True if D equals 1 or the discriminant of a quadratic field; false otherwise. D can be input in factored form as for arithmetic functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples and timing notes for counting fundamental discriminants up to large bounds. Library syntax: long isfundamental(GEN D).

rubrics_metrics.name: ispolygonal: test for s-gonal numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: True if integer x is an s-gonal number (s>2 t_INT). Optional &N set to n if x is n-th s-gonal number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: long ispolygonal(GEN x, GEN s, GEN *N = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: ispower: detect k-th powers and maximal exponent
rubrics_metrics.description: If k given, returns 1 if x is a k-th power, else 0. If k omitted (allowed only for integers/fractions), returns maximal k ≥ 2 such that x = n^k or 0 if none. For t_FFELT, use specific k computed from field parameters. Optional &n returns k-th root.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different types have different meanings of 'k-th power' (see issquare). Library syntax: long ispower(GEN x, GEN k = NULL, GEN *n = NULL) and gisanypower for GP-specific variant.

rubrics_metrics.name: ispowerful: powerful integer test
rubrics_metrics.description: True if integer x is powerful (valuation at all primes dividing x > 1), false otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples. Library syntax: long ispowerful(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: isprime: rigorous primality testing and flag options
rubrics_metrics.description: True (1) if x is a prime number, false (0) otherwise. Proves or disproves rigorously that a number is prime (potentially slow for large primes). If flag=0 uses combination of BPSW pseudoprime test, Selfridge 'p−1' if x−1 smooth, APRCL for medium-size (<1500 bits), ECPP for large x. flag=1 uses Selfridge-Pocklington-Lehmer p−1 only; flag=2 APRCL only; flag=3 ECPP only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ispseudoprime for quick compositeness check; use primecert for a primality certificate. Function is vectorized over vectors/matrices. Library syntax: GEN gisprime(GEN x, long flag). Time examples and warnings about slowness for very large primes provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: isprimepower / isprimepower: detect prime powers
rubrics_metrics.description: If x = p^k with p prime (k>0), return k else 0. Optional &n set to p when true.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: long isprimepower(GEN x, GEN *n = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: ispseudoprime: strong pseudoprime tests and flags
rubrics_metrics.description: True (1) if x is a strong pseudo prime (per implementation), false (0) otherwise. If returns false x is composite; if true it's highly likely prime. flag=0: checks no small prime divisors up to 101 and BPSW pseudo-prime (Rabin-Miller base 2 + Lucas test). flag>0: checks strong Miller-Rabin pseudo prime for 'flag' randomly chosen bases (with end-matching to catch sqrt(-1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No known composites pass the default test; all composites ≤ 2^64 are correctly detected. Use isprime for rigorous proof. Library syntax: GEN gispseudoprime(GEN x, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: ispseudoprimepower: detect pseudo-prime powers
rubrics_metrics.description: If x = p^k where p is pseudo-prime per ispseudoprime (k>0), return k, else 0. Optional &n set to p when true. For bases n ≤ 2^64 behavior is exact; for n>2^64 the function may return 1 even if n composite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: long ispseudoprimepower(GEN x, GEN *n = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: issquare: square detection across types
rubrics_metrics.description: True if x is a square, false otherwise. Meaning depends on type: all complex numbers are squares, non-negative reals are squares, exact types (INT, FRAC, INTMOD) checked accordingly. For polynomials checks depend on characteristic handling. Optional &n returns a square root.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For t_POLMOD only supports t_INTMOD encoding finite fields and assumes modulus irreducible/prime without checking. Library syntax: long issquareall(GEN x, GEN *n = NULL) and long issquare(GEN x) deprecated GP-specific variants noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: issquarefree: squarefree test for integers and polynomials
rubrics_metrics.description: True if x is squarefree, false otherwise. x can be integer or polynomial with coefficients in an integral domain. A polynomial is declared squarefree if gcd(x, x') = 1; non-zero polynomial with inexact coefficients considered squarefree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note possible inconsistency with factor which first rounds input before factoring. Integer may be input in factored form. Examples and timing notes for counting squarefree integers given. Library syntax: long issquarefree(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: istotient: check whether x is Euler totient value
rubrics_metrics.description: True if x = φ(n) for some integer n, false otherwise. Optional &N sets N = n if exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples. Library syntax: long istotient(GEN x, GEN *N = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: kronecker: Kronecker symbol extension & special rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Kronecker symbol (x|y) for integers x,y; extension of Legendre symbol by total multiplicativity with special rules for y = 0, -1, 2: (x|0)=1 if |x|=1 else 0; (x|-1)=1 if x≥0 else -1; (x|2)=0 if x even, 1 if x≡1 or -1 mod 8, -1 if x≡3 or -3 mod 8.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: long kronecker(GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: lcm: least common multiple behavior across types
rubrics_metrics.description: Least common multiple of x and y such that lcm(x,y)*gcd(x,y)=x*y up to units. If y omitted and x vector returns lcm of components. For integer arguments return non-negative lcm. For vector/matrix types LCM taken recursively with type-preserving rules and lcm not commutative on these types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note lcm(v) differs from iterative reduction; the implementation uses divide-and-conquer tree and is more efficient for large vectors, especially with GMP kernel. Examples and timing given. Library syntax: GEN glcm0(GEN x, GEN y = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: logint: integer logarithm rounding and z output
rubrics_metrics.description: Return largest integer e such that b^e ≤ x for integer b>1 and x>0. Optional &z set to b^e. Useful to compute number of digits with 1 + logint(x,b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May replace floor(log(x)/log(b)) which may misround; examples provided. Library syntax: long logint0(GEN x, GEN b, GEN *z = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: moebius: Möbius function
rubrics_metrics.description: Moebius µ-function of |x|; x must be non-zero integer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: long moebius(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: nextprime / precprime: nearest pseudoprime search
rubrics_metrics.description: nextprime(x) finds smallest pseudoprime ≥ x (returns x if x is pseudoprime). precprime(x) finds largest pseudoprime ≤ x (returns 0 if x ≤ 1). Results may be pseudoprimes; to rigorously prove primality use isprime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works on any real-type x. Library syntaxes: GEN nextprime(GEN x) and GEN precprime(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: numdiv: number of divisors
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of divisors of |x| for integer x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN numdiv(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: omega / bigomega: count distinct and total prime factors
rubrics_metrics.description: omega(x) returns number of distinct prime divisors of |x|; bigomega returns number with multiplicity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given using factor output. Library syntax: long omega(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: prime: nth prime (practical limits & performance)
rubrics_metrics.description: prime(n) returns nth prime number. Uses checkpointing and a naive O(n) algorithm and will need ~30 minutes for n up to 10^11; ensure gp started with primelimit at least sqrt(n log(n log n)) (documentation hints).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example retrieving prime(10^9). Library syntax: GEN prime(long n).

rubrics_metrics.name: primecert: produce PARI primality certificate (ECPP or N-1)
rubrics_metrics.description: If N is prime return a PARI Primality Certificate; else return 0. flag=0 (default) returns ECPP certificate (Atkin-Morain). flag=1 (very slow) returns N-1 (Pocklington-Lehmer) certificate. ECPP certificate structure: vector where each component is length-5 vector [Ni, ti, si, ai, Pi] with constraints listed (Ni positive, ti integer, si divides mi=Ni+1−ti, qi=mi/si > (Ni^(1/4)+1)^2, etc.) and Pi an affine point on y^2 = x^3 + a_i x + b_i with specified properties. The N-1 certificate is a pair [N, C] with constraints on prime divisors pi of N−1 and requires product of certain powers > N^(1/3) and Billhart-Lehmer-Selfridge criterion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theorem: existence of data with q>(N^(1/4)+1)^2 and suitable point properties implies N is prime. ECPP certificates supported for export; N-1 export not implemented. Providing partial factorizations may cause warnings but does not invalidate certificate if completed. Library syntax: GEN primecert(GEN N, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: primecertexport: format ECPP certificate for printing/export
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns a string suitable for print/write to display a primality certificate from primecert. format=0 human-readable (default), 1 Primo format 4, 2 MAGMA format. Currently only ECPP certificates supported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example prints human-readable, Primo and Magma outputs. N-1 certificates not yet implemented for export (error shown). Library syntax: GEN primecertexport(GEN cert, long format).

rubrics_metrics.name: primecertisvalid: validate PARI ECPP certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: Verifies if cert is a valid PARI ECPP primality certificate as described in primecert. Returns 1 if valid, 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows detection of tampering and invalid certificates. Library syntax: long primecertisvalid(GEN cert).

rubrics_metrics.name: primepi / primes: prime counting and list of primes
rubrics_metrics.description: primepi(x) returns number of primes p ≤ x. primes(n) returns row vector of first n primes or primes in interval if n is a 2-component vector [a,b].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: primepi uses naive O(x) algorithm with checkpointing; ensure primelimit large enough. Examples given. Library syntaxes: GEN primepi(GEN x) and GEN primes0(GEN n).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfbclassno: ordinary class number of quadratic order & algorithmic choices
rubrics_metrics.description: Computes ordinary class number of quadratic order of discriminant D for 'small' D. If D>0 or flag=1 use O(|D|^{1/2}) algorithm (compute L(1,χD)). If D<0 and flag=0 use O(|D|^{1/4}) algorithm (Shanks). Function gives unconditionally correct results for |D|<2·10^{10} in Shanks branch but may be incorrect for larger D if class group has many cyclic factors; recommend double-check with quadclassunit (assumes GRH). Note routine does not compute number of classes of primitive binary forms (narrow class number) — a conversion formula is given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance guidance: quadclassunit may be faster for some D ranges. Examples and warnings about correctness and expectations. Library syntax: GEN qfbclassno0(GEN D, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfbcompraw: compose binary quadratic forms without reduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Composition of binary quadratic forms x and y without reduction of result; useful to compute generating element of an ideal. Result undefined if discriminants differ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN qfbcompraw(GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfbhclassno: Hurwitz class number with GRH assumption for large x
rubrics_metrics.description: Hurwitz class number of x when x≥0 and x≡0 or 3 (mod 4); 0 otherwise. For x>5·10^5 assume GRH and use quadclassunit with default parameters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given. Library syntax: GEN hclassno(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfbnucomp / nudupl: NUCOMP-based composition & duplication algorithms
rubrics_metrics.description: Composition of primitive positive definite binary quadratic forms using Shanks' NUCOMP and NUDUPL algorithms; L is a positive constant for optimization (optimal L = |D/4|^{1/4}). Result undefined if discriminants differ. Implementation slower than generic routine for small D and faster when D has about 45 bits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntaxes: GEN nucomp(GEN x, GEN y, GEN L) and GEN nudupl(GEN x, GEN L) for doubling.

rubrics_metrics.name: qfbnupow: power of quadratic form via NUCOMP/NUDUPL
rubrics_metrics.description: n-th power of primitive positive definite binary quadratic form x using NUCOMP/NUDUPL; optional L parameter should equal sqrt-nint(abs(D)>>2,4) for optimal speed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Slower than generic for small discriminant, faster for large (D≈2^{45}). Library syntax: GEN nupow(GEN x, GEN n, GEN L = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfbpowraw: n-th power without reduction
rubrics_metrics.description: n-th power of binary quadratic form x computed without reduction (using qfbcompraw). n must be non-negative and < 2^31.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN qfbpowraw(GEN x, long n).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfbprimeform: prime binary quadratic form of given discriminant and first coefficient
rubrics_metrics.description: Return prime binary quadratic form of discriminant x whose first coefficient is p where |p| is prime. p=±1 returns the unit form. Error if x not quadratic residue mod p, or if x<0 and p<0. Negative definite t_QFI not implemented. For x>0, distance component set to zero according to current precision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN primeform(GEN x, GEN p, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: qfbred: reduction of binary quadratic form & flag toggles
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduces binary quadratic form x (updating Shanks's distance function if x is indeﬁnite). Binary digits of flag are toggles meaning: 1 perform a single reduction step; 2 don't update Shanks's distance. (Documentation continues beyond chunk.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional optional parameters d, isd, sd exist (documentation truncated in this chunk). Library syntax: described as qfbred(x, {flag = 0}, {d}, {isd}, {sd}).
